newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Quotes from day of Israeli-Palestinian clashes.
newsitem.headline: Quotes from day of Israeli-Palestinian clashes.

text.p: Unprecedented gunfights between Israelis and Palestinians that killed more than 50 people in two days evoked an outpouring of comments on Thursday on both sides.
Uzi Dayan, Israeli Central Commander:
"Since this morning the central command is in a state of emergency."
Moshe Katzav, acting Israeli prime minister:

"In the last two hours, the army chief, the Shin Bet chief, the adviser to the prime minister Yitzhak Molho, the defence minister, the prime minister -- all of them spoke with (Palestinian President) Yasser Arafat and he promised them all he would act. If he cannot, then he cannot be a leader."
Yitzhak Mordechai, Israeli Defence Minister:
In reference to Israel's decision to open a tourist tunnel in Old Jerusalem: "I don't know whether to say with finality...if all considerations were taken into account."
Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, Palestinian Cabinet Secretary:
"What's going on is a result of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's government's policies to use force against the Palestinian demonstrators. They are killing the peace process."
David Bar-Illan, adviser to Netanyahu:

"Any kind of danger of security being discarded means the collapse of the peace process. Unless Arafat, unless the Palestinian Authority...discard the war option altogether, we are not going to be able to continue with the peace process."
Ahmed Tibi, adviser to Arafat:
"The writing was on the wall."
Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, Director-General of Palestinian Presidency:
"We don't object to meetings with Israeli officials but on condition they lead to serious implementation of peace accords, to halting of Israeli violations."
Edward Abington, U.S. Consul General in Jerusalem:
"We are trying as hard as we can, the United States, to stop the violence and get the two sides back talking about their problems."
Shimon Peres, Israeli Labour Party leader:

"What was until now politically doubtful is starting to become a reality full of blood, covered in blood...We must immediately arrive at a ceasefire, to a dialogue with substance, because mere words will not be of any use at this difficult hour."
Akeed Abu Fakhr, Palestinian Force 17 Ramallah commander:
"We want to invest in the victory of what happened yesterday and today. We must give negotiations now a chance... Please go back to your homes."
Moshe Shahal, former Israeli Labour Party police minister:

"I think that Netanyahu proves every day with his deeds a lack of wisdom, a lack of ability...I want the thing to be said out loud, 'Bibi' Netanyahu is not suitable to be the prime minister of Israel."
Zeev Schiff, Israeli military commentator:

"Not all heads of security organs -- those involved in the affairs of the territories and Palestinians -- were asked their opinions whether it was desirable now to open the tunnel...It is incorrect that the Shin Bet gave its explicit approval."
A Palestinian policeman to demonstrators:
"Stop throwing stones. This will not help now."
Chanting Palestinian demonstrators:
"We are going to Jerusalem."
